## What changed

**A concurrent `apt-get update` killed a nineteen-step climb before it began.**
The run stopped on its very first action with exit 100, and the readiness check
one second earlier had said apt was free. Both were true: `apt-get update`
takes `/var/lib/apt/lists/lock`, the check looked at
`/var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend`, and those are different files. Something else —
`apt-daily`, `unattended-upgrades`, a person in another session — was holding
the one that mattered.

Reproduced rather than guessed: two `apt-get update` at once give exactly
`E: Could not get lock /var/lib/apt/lists/lock`, exit 100, while `fuser` on the
dpkg lock returns "nobody". Both halves are fixed. The check now examines every
lock apt takes and names which one is held and by which pid. And `apt-get
update` waits for the other process instead of dying — up to six attempts,
twenty seconds apart, announcing each wait, because a silent pause is
indistinguishable from a hang.

Only lock contention is retried. Any other failure is raised immediately: a
retry on top of "the repository is not signed" hides the reason and wastes the
time it took to find it.

The fixture that should have caught this was keyed on a hand-written copy of
the lock path; it is now keyed on the list of locks itself, so the two cannot
drift apart in silence — the same lesson the migration query taught earlier.
